newsitem.title: UK: Transco tenders to sell 4.7 TWh storage gas.
newsitem.headline: Transco tenders to sell 4.7 TWh storage gas.

text.p: Transco, the gas transport and pipeline arm of BG plc, will sell up to 4.7 teraWatt hours (Twh) of Residual Surplus Gas from storage by tender, the company announced.
Confirmation of intention to tender is due by Tuesday afternoon, it added.

Transco is inviting tenders for 4,713,276,803 kiloWatt hours (kWh) of gas from Rough storage, and a further 184,000,001 kWh of gas from Partington, although the total volume sold will not be more than the volume offered at Rough.
The total volume offered there is equivalent to a little over 160 million therms.

The tender will reflect the recent modifications, numbers 128 and 157, to the Network Code, the rulebook governing use of the pipeline system by both Transco and gas shippers. These modifications were approved by industry regulator Ofgas at the end of June.

The main difference to the original tender to sell off storage gas caused by the modifications is that successful bidders will have the option to take gas either in storage or at the National Balancing Point (NBP). Before the modifications were approved, the gas could only change hands within storage.
Transco has issued four separate options for tenderers looking to take gas.
First, the transaction will take place as a Storage Gas Transfer either at Rough or Partington on August 1.
Second, transfer will take place at the NBP, with gas transferred daily and at a flat daily rate from August 1 to 31.
Third, transfer will take place as a Storage Gas Transfer in the same way as in option one, but with transfer taking place on September 1.
And fourth, transfer will take place at the NBP in the same way as in option two, with transfer taking place at a flat daily rate throughout September.
Confirmation of intention to tender is due to be received by Transco by 1500 GMT on Tuesday, with sealed bids to be received by 1500 GMT on July 11.
Successful bidders will be notified by 0500 GMT on July 15. The minimum bid size will be 3,000,000 kWh, or slightly over 100,000 therms.
